cohort: The study included 51 infants diagnosed with neonatal sepsis and 50 neonates without sepsis who served as a control group.
finding: Serum interleukin-33 levels are significantly elevated in neonatal sepsis and show potential as a novel diagnostic marker and a useful tool for predicting prognosis.
followup_time: 7 days (after onset of sepsis for cases; 3 days postpartum for controls)
